purpose: Flurbiprofen is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis. It can also be used to reduce pain from other conditions like muscle aches or menstrual cramps. An eye drop form is used before certain eye surgeries to keep the pupil from getting smaller during the procedure.
how_it_works: Flurbiprofen works by blocking certain chemicals in your body called prostaglandins, which cause pain and inflammation. By reducing these chemicals, the medication helps decrease swelling, redness, and pain. Think of it like turning down the volume on your body's pain and inflammation signals.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, heartburn, or stomach pain. Some people may also experience headaches, dizziness, or diarrhea. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of stomach bleeding, ulcers, heart attack, or stroke, especially with long-term use. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, heart disease, high blood pressure, or if you are pregnant. Avoid taking it with other NSAIDs like ibuprofen or naproxen unless your doctor says it is okay.
typical_dosing: For arthritis, the usual adult dose is 200 to 300 mg per day, split into 2 to 4 smaller doses throughout the day. Your doctor will prescribe the lowest dose that works for you. Always take it exactly as your doctor or pharmacist instructs.
